digest.component_or_area: inbound link-removal path; peer-confirmation record persistence
propositions: Managed links marked locally by managed_refs cannot be distinguished from peer-deleted links when outbound ADD dedup on (vendor_type, target_key) prevents the link from ever being pushed, allowing inbound removal records to delete never-pushed local links.
Inbound removal records must be declined for managed-but-never-peer-confirmed links and declined removals must be logged and surfaced in pass summary to prevent silent data loss.

Peer-confirmation must be durable and survive SNAPSHOT compaction, persisted as a sidecar record keyed by (source_local_id, target_local_id, relation) containing Jira linkId and confirmed_pass/confirmed_at.
Removals must converge normally for links proven carried by the peer via either successful outbound ADD application or observation in an authoritative snapshot fetch.
Completeness is a trichotomy: absent issuelinks=unobserved, issuelinks=[]authoritatively-empty, populated=evidence; partial/paginated reads must never become deletion evidence.
Fail-open design: unopenable or corrupt peer-confirmation store disables decline logic and restores pre-a4bd behaviour, making confirmation an optimization of safety rather than a precondition.
